name: Global deep value equity
plain: Holds the lowest-valued listed companies worldwide on earnings, book value and cash flow, and earns the return as valuations normalise. Returns come in bursts, and the strategy can lag growth markets for several years.

name: Quality at a reasonable price
plain: Owns companies with high returns on capital and strong balance sheets, bought only at a discount to estimated intrinsic value. The valuation discipline limits drawdowns compared with paying any price for quality.

name: Value factor investing
plain: Tilts a low-cost index portfolio towards shares that are cheap on standard valuation measures. The value premium is long-term and cyclical, so it depends on holding through extended periods of underperformance.

name: Sovereign bond relative value
plain: Buys government bonds whose yields look high against the growth and inflation outlook and sells those that look expensive. Returns come from spreads converging rather than from the direction of rates.

name: Distressed debt investing
plain: Buys the bonds of financially stressed companies below the value expected from a restructuring or recovery. Returns depend on legal outcomes and recovery rates, and positions can be illiquid for long periods.

name: FX value investing
plain: Holds currencies trading below fair value on purchasing power parity and sells those above it. Deviations close slowly, so this is a multi-year position that can move against the holder in the short term.

name: REIT discount to NAV investing
plain: Buys listed property companies trading below the appraised value of their assets. The discount tends to narrow through buybacks, asset sales or takeovers, although property values remain sensitive to interest rates.

name: Private equity secondaries
plain: Buys existing stakes in private equity funds from investors who need liquidity, usually at a discount to reported net asset value. The discount and shorter remaining fund life support returns compared with new commitments.

name: Long-term quality growth equity
plain: Holds companies that can reinvest earnings at high returns on capital for many years, so returns compound with earnings growth. Valuations are high, which makes the strategy sensitive to rising interest rates.

name: AI supply chain thematic equity
plain: Owns the suppliers of AI infrastructure, from semiconductors and memory to power, cooling and data centres. Returns follow hyperscaler capital spending, so the strategy is volatile when spending guidance changes.

name: Thematic growth ETF allocation
plain: Spreads exposure across structural growth themes such as automation, clean energy and digital payments through low-cost funds. Diversifying across themes reduces the impact of any single theme falling out of favour.

name: Core digital asset allocation
plain: Holds a small, regularly rebalanced core of the largest digital assets, mainly Bitcoin and Ether. Rebalancing captures part of the volatility, but past cycles have included drawdowns of more than 70%.

name: Pre-IPO growth equity
plain: Invests in late-stage private companies ahead of a listing. Returns depend on the IPO window staying open, and valuations can be reset sharply when public market multiples fall.

name: Treasury bill laddering
plain: Rolls a ladder of short-dated government bills so that a tranche matures every few weeks. It earns close to the policy rate with almost no price volatility or credit risk.

name: Barbell bond allocation
plain: Combines short-dated bonds for liquidity with long-dated bonds for yield and duration. The mix earns more than short bonds alone while limiting losses compared with holding only long bonds.

name: Investment grade bond laddering
plain: Holds high-quality corporate bonds with staggered maturities, so part of the portfolio matures each year and is reinvested at current yields. It provides predictable income with moderate interest rate risk.

name: Dividend quality investing
plain: Owns companies whose dividends are well covered by free cash flow and backed by strong balance sheets. Covered dividends are cut less often, which supports both income and capital in downturns.

name: Covered call writing
plain: Holds a portfolio of shares and sells call options against it to collect premium. The premium adds income and cushions small falls, but it caps gains in strong rallies.

name: Real asset income investing
plain: Collects contracted rent and regulated cash flows from property, utilities and infrastructure. Income is relatively stable, although asset values fall when real interest rates rise.

name: Direct lending
plain: Lends directly to mid-sized companies through floating-rate senior loans, earning a premium over syndicated loans. Reported volatility is low partly because the loans are valued infrequently, so it understates the true risk.

name: Multi-asset income ETF allocation
plain: Combines income funds across bonds, dividend equities and listed property. Drawing income from several asset classes keeps the yield steadier than any single source.

name: Stablecoin yield lending
plain: Earns interest by lending stablecoins on lending platforms, at yields above money market rates. The holder bears platform default risk and the risk of a stablecoin losing its peg.

name: Cross-asset trend following
plain: Follows sustained price trends across equity, bond, currency and commodity futures, long or short. It has historically gained during extended sell-offs, which makes it a strong diversifier for equity portfolios.

name: Equity momentum investing
plain: Rotates into the shares with the strongest returns over the past six to twelve months. The premium is well documented, but the strategy can suffer sharp losses when market leadership reverses.

name: Sector rotation strategy
plain: Moves between sector funds as relative strength and the economic cycle shift market leadership. Returns depend on leadership persisting long enough to cover trading costs.

name: FX trend following
plain: Follows sustained moves in major currency pairs, which are often driven by diverging interest rate policy. It performs best when central banks move in different directions.

name: Commodity trend following
plain: Follows supply-driven price trends in energy, metals and agricultural futures. Commodity trends tend to persist because supply takes time to respond to prices.

name: Crypto trend following
plain: Holds digital assets during uptrends and moves to cash when the trend turns. Exiting in downtrends has historically avoided much of the drawdown, at the cost of missing sharp rebounds.

name: Fixed income trend following
plain: Follows trends in government bond futures across major markets. It benefits from sustained rate cycles in either direction, both hiking and cutting.

name: Variance risk premium harvesting
plain: Sells short-dated index options when implied volatility is above the volatility the market is likely to realise. It earns steady premium most of the time, with occasional large losses in sharp sell-offs.

name: Earnings long straddle
plain: Buys options before results when the implied move is small against the stock's history of earnings reactions. Returns come from a minority of large moves, so results are uneven.

name: VIX roll yield capture
plain: Earns the decline of VIX futures towards spot when the futures curve is in contango. Returns are steady in calm markets, but losses are severe when volatility spikes.

name: Long gamma scalping
plain: Owns options and repeatedly hedges their market exposure, profiting when realised moves exceed what the options cost. It gains most in turbulent markets.

name: Index dispersion trading
plain: Sells volatility on an index and buys volatility on its constituents, profiting when stocks move independently rather than together. Losses occur when correlation rises sharply, as it does in sell-offs.

name: FX volatility carry trade
plain: Sells currency options when implied volatility exceeds realised volatility. It earns premium in stable markets and loses in sudden currency moves.

name: Crypto volatility arbitrage
plain: Trades the difference between implied and realised volatility in digital asset options. Mispricing is frequent, but liquidity and exchange risk are material.

name: Oil event volatility trading
plain: Buys oil options ahead of supply events when implied volatility is low against past reactions to similar events. Most positions expire with small losses, offset by large gains in genuine disruptions.

name: Equity pairs trading
plain: Buys one stock and sells a close peer when their price relationship moves well outside its historical range. Returns are largely independent of the direction of the market.

name: Crypto basis trading
plain: Buys digital assets in the spot market and sells futures at a premium, earning the basis as the two prices converge. The position is market neutral but carries exchange and counterparty risk.

name: Convertible bond arbitrage
plain: Buys convertible bonds that are cheap relative to their embedded option and hedges the equity exposure by selling the shares. Returns come from the valuation gap and from trading volatility.

name: ETF arbitrage
plain: Trades small gaps between ETF prices and the value of their underlying holdings. Returns are small and steady, and they depend on fast, low-cost execution.

name: Yield curve butterfly trading
plain: Trades kinks in the yield curve, buying cheap maturities and selling expensive ones, while staying neutral to the overall level of rates.

name: Commodity spread trading
plain: Trades related contracts, such as different delivery months or refined products against crude, when their price spread moves beyond its normal range.

name: Index futures mean reversion
plain: Takes positions against short, sharp index moves that news or data do not explain, expecting a partial reversal within days.

name: Merger arbitrage
plain: Buys the shares of takeover targets below the agreed offer price and holds them until the deal closes. The spread is earned in most cases, with sharp losses if a deal is blocked.

name: Post-earnings announcement drift
plain: Holds shares that beat earnings expectations by a wide margin, as prices tend to keep adjusting for several weeks after the announcement.

name: Scenario-based hedged allocation
plain: Builds positions in the assets most exposed to the events identified by Rehyn's scenario engine, with hedges against the main risks. Positions change as the event outlook changes.

name: Central bank event trading
plain: Positions in rates around central bank meetings, based on how markets reacted to comparable decisions and guidance.

name: Special situations credit investing
plain: Trades corporate bonds around refinancings, spin-offs and rating changes, where forced selling or index rules create temporary mispricing.

name: Supply shock event trading
plain: Trades disruptions in energy and agriculture, using comparable historical episodes to estimate the size and duration of the price response.

name: Catastrophe bond investing
plain: Earns insurance premiums by holding bonds that lose principal only if a specified natural disaster occurs. Returns are largely unrelated to financial markets, with sudden losses in a major catastrophe.

name: G10 FX carry trade
plain: Holds high-yielding G10 currencies against low-yielding ones and earns the interest rate differential. Returns are steady in calm markets but reverse quickly when risk appetite falls.

name: Yield curve steepener trade
plain: Positions for short-term yields to fall faster than long-term yields, which typically happens when central banks begin cutting rates.

name: Commodity roll yield carry
plain: Holds commodity futures where the curve is in backwardation, earning the roll return as contracts converge towards higher spot prices.

name: Gold real yield allocation
plain: Sizes gold holdings from real yields, the US dollar and central bank purchases, the main drivers of the gold price over the past two decades.

name: Risk parity allocation
plain: Allocates across equities, bonds and commodities so that each contributes a similar share of portfolio risk, using leverage on the lower-risk assets. It is vulnerable when stocks and bonds fall together, as in 2022.

name: Short-duration high yield investing
plain: Holds high-yield bonds with short maturities, earning high coupons with limited exposure to interest rates. Defaults are the main source of loss.

name: Global macro futures overlay
plain: Takes directional views on growth, inflation and policy through equity index, bond and currency futures.

name: Autocallable note laddering
plain: Holds structured notes with staggered maturities that pay a fixed coupon and redeem early if markets hold up. The investor bears the equity loss if the index falls below the barrier.

name: Inflation-linked infrastructure investing
plain: Owns infrastructure assets whose revenue is contractually linked to inflation, such as regulated utilities and toll roads.

name: Tail risk hedging
plain: Holds out-of-the-money index options that cost a small premium in most years and pay out sharply in a crash.

name: Strategic gold allocation
plain: Holds a fixed allocation to gold as a store of value and a diversifier against currency debasement and geopolitical risk.

name: Safe haven currency allocation
plain: Holds currencies that tend to strengthen in risk-off periods, such as the Swiss franc and the Japanese yen.

name: Long volatility hedging
plain: Holds a rolling position in volatility futures that rises sharply when market stress increases. The roll cost is a drag in calm markets.

name: Minimum volatility equity
plain: Owns the least volatile stocks in the market, giving equity exposure with smaller drawdowns at the cost of lagging in strong rallies.

name: Long-duration Treasury hedge
plain: Holds long-dated Treasuries, which tend to rise when growth fears push yields down. The hedge fails when inflation drives stocks and bonds down together.
